In general, the expansion of services provided by Big Horn County for any population increase (including in-migrants due to coal mining) will not have to be large. The library, county hospital, public health, ambulance, and mental health services will need to expand somewhat to meet the needs of a growing population. The required expansion will be made larger by the fact that several facilities are presently at full capacity (Westmoreland Resources, 1975 f) and by the presence of Westmoreland construction and operating forces. However, impacts associated with these demands will be relatively small because community-serving facilities can expand more slowly than household-serving facilities, and because many services, such as fire protection and law enforcement, are concentrated in the municipality of Hardin where the majority of new residents are expected to live.
Services similar to those provided by the county are supplied for Indian residents by the BIA, IHS and the Tribal Government. Because there is assumed to be no net Indian migration, these special services will expand only to meet normal population increase. This enlargement would be required regardless of coal development. The required expansion will be large for services such as education and health because of the more than 100 percent increase in Indian population during the project period. Specifically, the Reservation hospital and other health services and the police department will require expansion.
